sentences.text: 2. This is a wholly misconceived petition filed by two petitioners claim to be heirs and legal representatives of Thakor Kalaji Madhaji.

The prayer made in the writ petition is to issue a direction to the respondent no. 1, namely the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Gandhinagar to decide the Thakor Kalaji Madhaji Since Decd. ... vs Special Land Acquisition Officer , ...

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101210039/
1 representation made by the petitioners dated 10.09.2020 for grant of compensation.

Further prayer is to issue direction to the respondents to determine just, fair and adequate compensation for acquisition of the land in question NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1366/2025 ORDER DATED:
05/02/2025 undefined forming part of Block No. 212, old Survey No. 59/2, 59/3 situated at Village Kudasan, Taluka and District Gandhinagar.

Considering the prayers made in the writ petition,
pertinent is to note that the acquisition proceedings were conducted with the publication of notifications dated 03.03.1966 and 21.04.1966 under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894; respectively.

As per own statement of the petitioners in paragraph '3.2.'of the writ petition, the award under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1894")
came to be passed on 01.03.1969.

It is contended in the said paragraph itself that a part of land bearing Survey No. 59/1 situated at Village Kudasan, District :
Gandhinagar was reflected as the land acquired in the award and then a statement of fact has been made to the effect that no notice under Section 12(2) of the Act, 1894 had been served to the petitioners till date and no compensation has been paid to the petitioners as well till date.
3.

We have strong exceptions to the said statement made by the petitioners in paragraph '3.2.' of the writ petition, inasmuch as, from a perusal of the description in the array of parties, the age of petitioner no. 1.1. is 51 years and the petitioner no. 1.2.
is aged about 47 years.

Once the acquisition proceedings were completed NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1366/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2025 undefined with the making of the award in the year 1969 as per own case of the petitioners, there was no question of issuance of notice under Section 12(2) of the Act, 1894 to the petitioners herein or payment of compensation to them.

4. Insofar as the original owner of the land in question at the time of acquisition, it is sought to be submitted in paragraph '3.7' of the writ petition that in 7/12 extract of the land in question, the occupancy of the father of the petitioner had been shown at the time of acquisition of the land in question.
The copy of 7/12 extract is starting from page '43' onwards.
The pedigree of the deceased occupant of the land in question has been filed at page '54' of the paper book, under the certificate issued by Kasba Talati, Gandhinagar.
The date of the death of the father of the petitioners namely, Thakor Kalaji Madhaji is mentioned therein as 27.01.2022.
From the above noted documents, atleast it is evident that the original occupant of the land in question was alive till 27.01.2022.
There is no averment in the writ petition that the father of the petitioners raised any dispute with regard to non-payment of compensation during his lifetime.
The representations made in the year 2020, are nothing but an after thought.

After the year 1969, when the award was made under Section 11 of the Act, 1894, there NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1366/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2025 undefined was no occasion to consider the claim of the original owner/occupant for non-payment of compensation under the award.

Even if the contention of the petitioners is accepted for a moment that their father had raised a dispute in the year 2020 with regard to non- payment of compensation during his lifetime, the dispute having Thakor Kalaji Madhaji Since Decd. ... vs Special Land Acquisition Officer , ... on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101210039/
2 been raised after more than 50 years cannot be entertained.

sentences.text: There was no reason for the father of the petitioners to keep silence for such a long time.
Even 7/12 extract appended with the writ petition does not reflect the name of the father of the petitioners and the statement in this regard is misleading.

4.1. It seems that much after acquisition proceedings were brought to their logical end, the father of the petitioners had sold the acquired land in the year 1996 which has led to initiation of the proceedings under the Gujarat Tenancy and Agricultural Land Act, resulting into filing of Special Civil Application No. 7120 of 2014.

entities.text: Gujarat Tenancy and Agricultural Land Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the tenancy proceedings were initiated with respect to a parcel of land which had not been acquired.

We may simply record that we do not find any reason to enter into the issue pertaining to the proceedings initiated under the Tenancy Act and we are not concerned with the tenancy proceedings initiated against the father of the petitioners in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1366/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2025 undefined present petition.
5.

However, from the facts brought on record of the present petition, it is evident that the acquisition proceedings were concluded with the making of the award under Section 11 of the Act,
1894 on 01.03.1969.
It is not permissible for the petitioners to raise any dispute with regard to determination or payment of compensation to their predecessor.
6. The present petition is, thus dismissed as misconceived.
No order as to cost.
